reviews.text:
Great scales, streamlined, stylish, and easy to use. Although made of glass, it is sturdy enough for every day use as long as you don't use it as a trampoline. So no jumping and jiggling it to try to get the thing to forget about that chocolate eclair and the two brownies you binged on!  And definitely drop kickicking it when you discover you have gained weight over the holidays.

I compared it to my weight on my doctors scales. My old scales were off by 3 lbs (they were 3 lbs lighter, so I have mixed feelings about tossing it out). This scale was dead on!  Guess I will have to lose those pesky 3 lbs. At least it has a bright, easy to read display so that my bleary old eyes can read it as I stumble into the bathroom each morning. Some days, I'm not sure that is such a good thing...Remember, if your self-image is inextricably tied up with the numbers on the scale, you need to weigh yourself first thing in the morning, at the same time each day, making sure to give that special someone a thrill by weighing yourself in the buff. And make sure to do this before you eat or drink. Even then, expect some fluctuations due to water weight. This is especially true for women due to hormonal variations, but if you happen to have grazed your way through a bowl of nachos, gobbled down a bag of salty chips, indulged in a pizza, or hit the local salt lick, expect to weigh more the next day regardless of your sex.

Note: I had chucked my old scales out weeks earlier, so when I first looked at my weight on this thing, my heart leaped for joy. Then, I realized the scale was in kilograms. It took multiple tries on my part to convert it to pounds, so hang in there. It will come around. Of course, you may not be all that happy when it does. I rather liked only weighing 45% of my normal weight.

reviews.title: Inconsistent and innaccurate. Or, on the bright side, great for those who want to be in denial about weight fluctuations
reviews.text:
As pretty and compact as this very nice-looking bathroom scale is, it has real problems with consistency and accuracy. Its fluid relationship with the truth is like being lied to by a cheating boyfriend about your weight every day. I ask it, "is my booty getting big?" and step on like a fool so it can tell me, "No, honey. You're as thin and beautiful as you were yesterday. And the day before. And the day before. And the day before that. No really. Exactly as thin and beautiful. Exactly. Exactly the same weight. To the ounce. You're holding a bowling ball now? Well, then that must mean that you're *losing* weight! Congratulations! Now go make me a sandwich."

Sadly, I have found this scale to be incapable of registering more than one reading per rough pound of body mass. If you're 102 lbs, give or take, it will tell you you're 102.4 until you edge up another half a pound or so, and then you'll jump up to register as 103.6. Never 103.2, 103.4, 103.8, it only knows 103.6. Adjust your footing and you're mysteriously and miraculously at exactly the same 102.4 from the day prior. Take off shoes or heavy clothing or put down your gargantuan smartphone whose manufacturer specs clock at half a pound in its kevlar advanced bomb suit case and see no change on the display. Not even a fraction of a pound. Pick up your purse and discover that it will cycle through the single weight it knows for each one-pound increment until it settles on its half-hearted guess. Put your purse back down and it refunds all that weight to you, save for one pound that is maybe some sort of rounding error or restocking fee, I'm not sure. Step off and back on and you're at your "original" weight, presumably having burned off that pesky pound doing step aerobics on your scale in search of an accurate reading.

Losing some weight? No you're not. Or maybe you are. It's a mystery. That 195.6 lb reading gotten by the second party tester you brought in to see if the scale would be more cooperative with another user will suddenly drop to 192.4, where it will stay until another pound or more is shed, and it will tell you then that he may or may not have moved into the next one-pound weight class. Or wait until he has a tantrum and shifts his left foot, at which point it will show another lost pound while mocking you under its breath.

I know that accuracy isn't that big a deal or terribly reliable with home bathroom scales, but this one truly seems like it's not even trying and is outright incapable of registering anything but preprogrammed weights, one per pound. I have no idea what I weigh right this second, but I know my doctor's office and gym scales agree that this one is playing head games with me. Either that, or I am gaining and losing brain mass trying to compute mathematical and histographical averages all the time in an attempt to divine my true weight from the scale that lives in my bathroom.

reviews.text:
I am not in the habit of writing reviews, but buyers should be aware of a few things. First, it is a piece of glass resting on top of four circular pads, so you will not be under illusions about why it is so cheap. Second, it is not obvious how to turn it on, the directions are incoherent. There is a battery compartment on the back with a tiny unlabeled switch inside of it. Left is Kg, right is Lbs.

I'm fairly indifferent to these aesthetic details. However, the display implies it has a precision to one decimal place, but it is not actually that precise. When I got back home from work I was exactly two pounds lighter. I picked up a textbook and was exactly three pounds heavier. Testing it again, it was bouncing back and forth by 1.2 pounds, sometimes giving one or the other answer.

I have not tested other scales yet to check for accuracy (if it is consistently biased by some number from actual weight), but it is the weight differences that really matter, so I do not hugely care and will just adjust it in my head. There is no way to reset the tare weight. It will still roughly do what I need to police myself in a downward or stationary trend. If you expect the scale to reveal some infallible, metaphysical truth about yourself, you should probably buy a more expensive one.

reviews.title: Sorely disappointed with the product -- Not working as advertised
reviews.text:
Sorely disappointed with the product -- definitely not consistent with some of the higher rated reviews on here. Perhaps I got a defective model?

At the very least, the scale only changes by increments of 0.8 (not 0.2 as advertised), and the scale readings are completely inconsistent for my weight. Sometimes it'll record a weight differential of up to 3 pounds in a span of 30 seconds!

I have even tested the accuracy of the weights by standing on the scale, recording it, and then measuring myself again holding a 15 pound dumbbell and checking if the displayed weight would increase by around 15 pounds. Instead, I've been getting huge fluctuations with this test. Sometimes my weight increases by around 12 pounds... sometimes it'll change by up to 19 pounds. It's not like my dumbbell is changing weight spontaneously.

I bodybuild and carefully track my weight, so I have no use for a scale that reads +/- 4-5 pounds on a given reading.

Again, I could just have a defective copy, but either way, I'll probably by a different scale from another vendor. Is there a way to refund this?

Scale came almost ten days after I started diet, and workouts, From my clothes being loose, I looked forward to seeing my progress. First time I stepped on the scale, it said I was 202 pounds.  Every since then ,while doing everything for it to work,scale has always put my weight over 200lbs even got a 220.  Tried everything to get it to work, rechecked the instructions, looked for info online but there doesn't seem to be a way to calibrate it properly or it just doesn't work. Threw out the box, so I am stuck with it.  My morale got hit harder than my wallet but I could have used that money towards another scale. Classic getting what you paid for scenario.

One day it told me that I gained 4 lbs in a day, when the analog scale showed no such change. This seems suspicious to me - it was a normal eating day so there is no reason why the reading on the scale should have fluctuated that much. It seems suspect to me. Otherwise so far it is functional (turns on and off just fine).

reviews.title: Went by the good reviews.
reviews.text:
Went by the good reviews..but unfortunately. what arrived is a piece of Made in China junk that looks like it cost $1.00 to manufacture. Yes I know everything is made in China, but when something is quality made you can tell.  This is poor quality. The glass piece on top pictured with the writing is backwards and the weights are inconsistent. It also arrived looking like it was used already as the glass is covered in smudges & fingerprints and what looked like splashes of water.
Returning it to Amazon, and this is the last scale I'm ordering from Amazon as this is now my second return.  I know they did not make the scale, but I feel some times may be better off buying in an actual store and paying a little more money instead of shipping & returning and then waiting for a refund. I never thought  a scale would be so problematic.

reviews.title: The best scale at the best price!! You want this scale!!!
reviews.text:
Came exactly as pictured. Works perfectly. You need to open the battery compartment and flip the switch to either kg or lb, and that's it, it's ready, just step on and it tells your weight. Very accurate as compared to my dr office scale. It came in a box representing a bunch of other styles, but the scale I received is solid black exactly as pictured when I purchased it.

This is an excellent scale, with a bright readout in a cool blue light. It is very smooth glass. I am extremely pleased with its simple design and operation. I have searched for a good scale at a good price trying multiple designs, this is amazing for the price I paid under $15!!!! I'd expect to pay upwards of $40 or more for this kind of scale. I am hoping it will last a very long time.

reviews.title: Look inside the battery compartment to turn it on... ;-)
reviews.text: It's fine, nice, big display that's easy to read...  BUT, you have to open the battery compartment and turn it on before the first use - which the instructions that come with it don't tell you.  I had actually started a return, because I thought it was either defective or the battery was dead (I wasn't willing to buy a battery for a scale that might be defective).  However, I got to thinking about it, and went back and got it out of the box to look at it a little closer... come to find out, my old eyes just couldn't see that little switch next to the battery without reading glasses!  It's OFF, and you switch it to either kg or lb to turn it on.  After that, all you do is step on it to turn it on... I took off one star for them not telling that in the instruction sheet - but otherwise, it's nice - and the price is great!

reviews.text: I LOVE this scale.  Terrific deal.  I notice some people having a few problems with this type of scale.  Make sure it is on a flat, smooth surface, and try not to move it around a lot.  Try to keep it out of the bathroom, as the wet environment is not ideal.  For some reason, this one seemed to weight us more consistently the longer we had it.  At first, we got variations of up to a little over a pound by repeated weighing back-to-back, but now repeated weighing seems to give a more consistent result.

reviews.title: Wrong deco print, other than that there's no complaints.
reviews.text:
I received the scale in a timely manner HOWEVER the online item's picture shows a rose deco on it and the one I received is plain black (no deco). I decided to keep it because it's a hassle to return it and wait for a new one since I plan to monitor my weight everyday with my new diet plan. As long as it wasn't an entirely different color with an ugly print on it, I was okay with it.

It came with the battery already installed. It's simple to turn on and easy to switch to LB or KG unit. Seems to work fine.

I would've given it 5 stars if they showed the correct deco on the product page. Other than that, it's a great price for $10.99!
